text: He describes reflux and heartburn as a feeling that the stomach is constantly full, with acid or fluid rising into the throat.
He says these symptoms often worsen after eating, and he describes common advice such as avoiding fried, heavily seasoned, fatty, or spicy foods.
He also mentions being told not to eat late at night, to sleep with the head elevated, and then to begin medication.
He lists treatments ranging from antacid products such as Gaviscon to tablets, and says severe symptoms may sometimes lead people to seek emergency care.
He says further testing may reveal Helicobacter pylori and suggests that this can be associated with worsening reflux symptoms.
He argues that symptoms may improve while taking medication but return when the medication is stopped.
He then links reflux, in his view, with irritable-bowel-type symptoms such as bloating, gas, constipation, and what he describes as poor absorption.
He further associates this with hair loss, osteoporosis, and low vitamin D.
He also mentions dental decay and gum or dental disease as possible related problems in his model.
He goes on to mention fatty liver and iron-deficiency anemia, again presenting these as connected conditions within his explanation.
He says that, in his view, these problems begin in the stomach and that reflux is a symptom of a broader digestive disorder rather than the main disease itself.
He urges people to address what he sees as the underlying cause instead of treating only the reflux symptoms, and says complications can continue if the underlying problem is not corrected.
He concludes that improving stomach function can, in his view, improve the rest of the body.
